alternate_names: Gurdwara Shaheed Baba Nihal Singh Ji
deities: Guru Granth Sahib (enshrined; Sikh gurdwaras do not house idol worship)
festivals: Shaheedi Jor Mela (June 3-5, anniversary of Baba Nihal Singh's martyrdom)

history.dynasty: None (community-built; managed by a gurdwara committee - modern institution)
history.period: 20th century (samadhi shrine founded 1953, per Swarajya reporting; Baba Nihal Singh lived c. 1803 to early 1900s)
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE. Gurudwara Talhan Sahib Ji, in Talhan village near Jalandhar (not in Jalandhar city itself), is dedicated to Shaheed Baba Nihal Singh Ji, a carpenter from neighbouring Dakoha village (born 1803) who served villagers by making and installing pulleys in drinking-water wells; local belief held that wells he worked on never dried up and gave sweet water. He died in an accident while installing a pulley; the villagers of Talhan built a samadhi (shrine) in his memory, later expanded into the present grand gurdwara, with a second samadhi for his associate Harnam Singh. The shrine established at the samadhi site dates to 1953 (verify). It is internationally famous as the 'Hawai Jahaz' (Airplane) Gurdwara: devotees seeking visas to travel abroad pray and offer toy aeroplanes (around 50-60 a week, per shrine authorities; the management once banned then reversed the ban). The gurdwara runs a modern charitable hospital, a school, continuous Akhand Path recitations, and langar. The annual Shaheedi Jor Mela (June 3-5) features kabaddi, volleyball, tug-of-war and gatka. In 2003 Talhan was the centre of a major Jat/Ramdasia (Dalit) dispute over representation on the gurdwara committee, culminating in protests and clashes - a widely reported chapter of the shrine's modern history.

name: Gurudwara Talhan Sahib Ji
town_description: Talhan is a small village (population ~2,940 per the 2011 Census) in Jalandhar district, Punjab, near the Jalandhar Cantonment, about 15 km from Jalandhar city on the Jalandhar-Ludhiana road. It is nationally known for the Talhan Sahib gurdwara and its annual Shaheedi Jor Mela. The village has shops, a bank, schools, a mosque and other gurdwaras besides the main shrine.

travel.airport: Adampur Airport (domestic, ~35 km) is nearest; Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~100 km) for international flights; then taxi/bus to Jalandhar and local transport to Talhan.
travel.railway: Jalandhar City station; Talhan is ~15 km away (a cab round trip was reported as ~30 km). Auto-rickshaws and taxis from Jalandhar city.
travel.road: On the Jalandhar-Ludhiana Road corridor; the gurdwara's own listing gives the address as Jalandhar Ludhiana Road, Jalandhar 144010.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Shaheedi Jor Mela (June 3-5) and Gurpurabs draw the biggest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listings conflict: the gurdwara's official site says 04:00 AM to 08:00 PM; TripAdvisor lists Mo-Su 12:00-23:59; another listing says 6:00 AM-9:00 PM daily (verify). Langar (free meal) is served; cover your head and remove shoes before entering.
